questions.prompt: What is the difference between merging with -X ours and running git restore --ours on a conflicted file?
options: -X ours decides only the conflicting hunks and keeps the other side's clean changes; restore --ours replaces the whole file with your version
They are the same; -X ours is a shortcut that applies restore --ours to every file
-X ours keeps the other branch's version; restore --ours keeps yours
restore --ours works during a merge; -X ours works only after it
